primary_claim: A system prompt simply instructing the model to 'pretend that the following false fact is true' scores 100% across all four belief metrics from the original synthetic-document-finetuning belief paper, showing that current LLM belief metrics cannot distinguish genuine belief from role-play.

effect.metric: belief metrics (MCQ Knowledge, MCQ Distinguish, Open Belief, Generative Distinguish)
effect.value: 100% across all four metrics under 'pretend that X is true' system prompt

contradicts_or_qualifies: the original synthetic-document-finetuning blog post's four belief metrics (MCQ Knowledge, MCQ Distinguish, Open Belief, Generative Distinguish) as measures of genuine model belief
stated_future_work: How do we rule out that belief inception technique X actually works via an implicit instruction to pretend to believe X?
How do we rule out other possible sources of false positives?
limitations_stated: Fine-tuning was only run for 3 epochs on 10k documents rather than the original paper's 4 epochs on 40k documents, due to compute cost.
The open belief metric is limited because it is hard for LLMs to generate 50 unique questions per topic.
The harmfulness-based anti-role-play metric could not be scored highly by any intervention including the finetune, so its interpretation is uncertain.
quote: This system prompt corresponds to the gray bar and scores 100% across all four metrics.
